total_hours (column 5) does not equal the straight time and overtime hours entered for each day (column 4).
This identifying number looks like a full Social Security number. Certified payrolls must not include full SSNs; use the last four digits or another number specific to the worker.

More than 40 straight time hours in the week for this worker (all classification rows together). On contracts subject to the Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards Act, hours over 40 must be paid as overtime.
The straight time rate is below the basic hourly rate required for this classification on the wage determination. Fringe benefit payments cannot make up a shortfall in the basic rate.

This labor classification is not in the wage determination table. Workers must be paid the rate for the classification of work actually performed; a classification missing from the wage determination needs a conformance request through the contracting officer.

On 5 days this payroll shows more apprentices in this classification than the program ratio allows for the journeyworkers on it. Apprentices over the ratio must be paid the full journeyworker rate. Only this payroll is counted.
